proof.text: Identify $C_A^\bullet(f)\otimes_A M$ with the complex in the statement as follows. For every product $g$ of generators, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], with base ring $A$, module $A$ and multiplicative set $\{1,g,g^2,\ldots\}$, gives $A_g\otimes_A M\cong M_g$ after the elementary identification $A\otimes_A M\cong M$. In this direction the map is $(a/g^n)\otimes m\mapsto am/g^n$. A finite product commutes with tensor here: the map to the product of tensors is induced by coordinate projections, and its inverse is the sum of the maps induced by coordinate inclusions; the identities follow from $\sum_S\iota_S\pi_S=1$. Apply these maps in each degree and $A\otimes_A M\cong M$ in degree zero. For a face localization from a subset $S$ to a larger subset $T$, both composites send $(a/g_S^n)\otimes m$ to the image of $am/g_S^n$ in $M_{g_T}$. Hence they commute with each alternating differential, with the same sign $(-1)^{a-1}$, and give a natural cochain isomorphism. For $r=0$ there are no localization factors: it is simply $A\otimes_A M\cong M$ in degree zero.

proof.text: Because $A$ is Noetherian, [lem-per-local-cohomology-noetherian-comparison] at $K=M[0]$ gives a natural isomorphism $R\Gamma_I(M[0])\to R\Gamma_Z(M[0])$, where $R\Gamma_I$ is computed by applying $\Gamma_I$ to a K-injective resolution. An injective resolution $M\to J^\bullet$ is a bounded-below complex of injectives, hence a K-injective resolution of $M[0]$, so [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification], applied to the additive functor $\Gamma_I$ of [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor] on $A$-modules (which have enough injectives), gives isomorphisms $H^j(R\Gamma_I(M[0]))\cong H^j(\Gamma_I(J^\bullet))=R^j\Gamma_I(M)=H_I^j(M)$, natural in $M$; they are $A$-linear because they are induced by an isomorphism of complexes of $A$-modules in $D(A)$. Compose the cohomology of the cochain isomorphism in Step 2, the isomorphism of Step 1, the inverse of the degree-$j$ cohomology of the comparison just given, and the identification $H^j(R\Gamma_I(M[0]))\cong H_I^j(M)$. The result is a natural $A$-linear isomorphism $H^j(C^\bullet(f;M))\cong H_I^j(M)$ for every $j\geq0$. Each factor is natural in module maps, so their composite is natural. If $r=0$, $I=(0)$, the torsion functor is the identity and its injective-resolution cohomology is $M$ in degree zero and zero in higher degrees, agreeing with the one-term complex.

title: Extended Cech model for ideal local cohomology
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $r\geq0$, and let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be an ideal. Let $M$ be any $A$-module and put $H_I^j(M)=R^j\Gamma_I(M)$ using [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. Define the cochain complex $C^\bullet(f;M)$ by $C^0=M$, by $C^q=\prod_{1\leq i_1<\cdots<i_q\leq r}M_{f_{i_1}\cdots f_{i_q}}$ for $1\leq q\leq r$, and by zero in other degrees; here $M_g$ denotes localization at $1,g,g^2,\ldots$. The differential into the component indexed by $i_1<\cdots<i_{q+1}$ is the sum of the localization maps from the components obtained by deleting $i_a$, with sign $(-1)^{a-1}$; for $q=0$ these are the maps from $M$. For every $j\geq0$ there is a natural $A$-linear isomorphism $H^j(C^\bullet(f;M))\cong H_I^j(M)$. When $r=0$ the complex is $M$ in degree zero and $I=(0)$.

theorem idealPowerTorsion_rightDerived_iso_cech
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (r : ℕ) (t : Fin r → R) (q : ℕ) :
    ∃ e : ∀ M : ModuleCat.{u} R,
      ((idealPowerTorsion (Ideal.span (Set.range t))).rightDerived q).obj M ≅
        (IdealTorsionCech.complex t M).homology q,
      ∀ {M N : ModuleCat.{u} R} (f : M ⟶ N),
        ((idealPowerTorsion (Ideal.span (Set.range t))).rightDerived q).map f ≫
            (e N).hom =
          (e M).hom ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (IdealTorsionCech.map t f) q
